description: prConcurrentLimit and prHourlyLimit are 0, which is Renovate's spelling of 'no limit'. They are NOT redundant lines to tidy away: deleting them restores the defaults of 10 concurrent and 2 per hour, so the throttle would come back silently.

What replaced them is the dashboard gate — for everything EXCEPT patches, which are exempt from it and open a pull request straight away (see the patch rule below). So patches are the one unbounded category: a pull request each, in whatever quantity a given day produces, each firing the full CI matrix. That is the deliberate shape of this config, not an oversight, but it is the thing to change first if the runners or the review queue ever suffer for it.

Generated build output ONLY. `android/**` and `ios/**` used to be listed wholesale, and that removed two of the four shipped platforms from dependency automation entirely: the AGP and google-services pins in android/build.gradle, the eleven androidx/Cordova versions in android/variables.gradle, the Gradle wrapper, and the iOS SPM graph — none of it watched by anything.

The reason that mattered more than a missed minor: ignorePaths is evaluated BEFORE package rules, so the vulnerabilityAlerts block below — the one category deliberately exempt from the dashboard gate — could not reach these files either. An advisory against androidx.webkit, which backs the WebView rendering an E2EE client, produced no branch, no PR and no dashboard row. Silent by construction.

What remains here is the copy of the web build each native shell embeds. Those trees are `pnpm build` output committed into the platform projects; a lockfile or manifest found inside one is a stale artefact, not a dependency, and updating it would be updating a build product.

A security fix must never sit behind a tick nobody has looked at, so this opts out of the dashboard gate and shortens the three-day soak to one day, the same minimumReleaseAge pnpm applies to every install. A delay is a risk here, but so is a release minutes old: one day still keeps out a version that is pulled within hours of publishing.

Security updates keep a pull request, so the `security` label below is applied and the CVE detail Renovate writes into prBodyNotes is kept. They do not automerge: 'Protect main' requires an approval and Renovate is not one of its bypass actors, so Renovate cannot complete a merge; a maintainer reviews and merges every update.

Patch updates skip the dashboard gate and open a pull request straight away. They do not automerge: 'Protect main' requires an approval and Renovate is not one of its bypass actors, so Renovate cannot complete a merge; a maintainer reviews and merges every update. A patch is the update type least likely to change behaviour, and minimumReleaseAge already holds every release for three days, so a version yanked hours after publishing never reaches a branch in the first place. Everything else waits for a tick under the top-level dependencyDashboardApproval.

additionalBranchPrefix puts these on renovate/patch-* instead of renovate/*, off the branch of a minor or major in the same group that is waiting for dashboard approval. Renovate composes branch names as branchPrefix + additionalBranchPrefix + branchTopic from the config resolved for each update, so a rule-level value is applied here and nowhere else.

packageRules.description: Angular and everything version-locked to it. These must move together — a partial bump leaves @angular/compiler-cli disagreeing with @angular/core and the build fails outright.
Nx and its plugins are released in lockstep and share a workspace version.
The Rust crypto WASM is coupled to the SDK that loads it; bumping one alone is how the E2EE init breaks.
Capacitor core, CLI and every plugin track one major — including the third-party ones, which peer-depend on @capacitor/core and break if they lag behind it.

description: `cap sync` writes each native plugin's pnpm virtual-store folder, version and peer suffix included, into ios/App/CapApp-SPM/Package.swift and android/capacitor.settings.gradle. Renovate only regenerates pnpm-lock.yaml, so without this every update to one of these packages failed the iOS and Android jobs, which run `cap sync` and then `git diff --exit-code` (#1630, #1641).

`cap sync` itself needs node_modules and a web build, neither of which exists after Renovate's lockfile-only install, so scripts/sync-native-plugin-paths.mjs derives the folder names from the lockfile alone. It runs once per branch, after the lockfile is updated, and commits only those two files. The command must match allowedCommands in .github/workflows/renovate.yml exactly, or Renovate refuses to run it and reports an artifact error on the pull request; a package missing from the lockfile fails the script and is reported the same way.
The package list is every package with a virtual-store path in those two files; extend it with the next native plugin.

packageRules.description: Brain (headless) and the CLI that generates the Helm components from it.
The icon component and its icon sets release in lockstep; one pull request keeps @ng-icons/core and the sets on the same version.
The Playwright runner and its browser package must match, or the browsers are re-downloaded and the versions disagree.
Vitest core and its coverage provider.
ESLint and the plugins that peer-depend on it.
Tailwind v4 is CSS-configured; its PostCSS plugin and the prettier plugin follow the same version.

The desktop shell is a separate package with its own lockfile and its own toolchain, so its updates must never be merged into a root group. TypeScript is the one exception, carved back out by the rule immediately below.

description: TypeScript follows Angular, not npm's latest, and electron/ follows the workspace. @angular/compiler-cli peer-depends on a single minor window — `>=6.0 <6.1` on Angular 22 — and pnpm only warns about an unmet peer rather than refusing to install, so a TypeScript minor bumped on its own would install cleanly and then fail in ngtsc, where it reads as an Angular bug rather than a dependency one.

This ceiling has to be widened BY HAND when an Angular major lands, and the Angular group's own PR is the moment to do it: read the new window off `pnpm view @angular/compiler-cli@<version> peerDependencies`. Until then, the Angular PR is what fails, not this one — Angular 23 requiring a TypeScript this rule still forbids shows up as a red Angular PR, not as a silently skipped update.

The desktop shell used to pin its own TypeScript 5.9 against the workspace's 6.x. That divergence was not free: @nx/js ships tsconfig codemods on every root TypeScript bump, they glob electron/tsconfig.json along with everything else, and the rewritten file then failed to parse under the older compiler — a breakage that arrived through a migration nobody ran against electron/, in a package CI builds separately. Both manifests now move as one version, in one branch.

ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: this rule must stay BELOW the electron shell rule. Renovate merges every matching packageRule in array order and the last one wins each key, so electron/'s TypeScript picks up groupName 'typescript' here only because this rule comes second. Move it above and the shell rule silently reclaims it into the 'electron shell' group — two branches, two versions, and the divergence is back with nothing to show it.
rangeStrategy pin keeps both manifests on an exact, textually identical version rather than a caret that could drift apart within the allowed window.

electron/tsconfig.json must stay on `module`/`moduleResolution` Node16 for this to hold. TypeScript 6 rejects the old node10 resolution outright (TS5107), so a revert to `Node` there breaks the desktop build the next time this rule fires.

The native build graphs, now that ignorePaths no longer hides them: Gradle (AGP, google-services, the eleven androidx/Cordova pins Capacitor writes into android/variables.gradle), the Gradle wrapper, and the iOS Swift package at ios/App/CapApp-SPM/Package.swift. No cocoapods rule — this project has no Podfile; Capacitor 8 generates SPM instead.

Grouped into ONE branch because Capacitor pins these versions as a set: androidx.webkit, androidx.core and the Cordova compatibility shims are chosen to match the @capacitor/android that ships them, and moving one of them alone is how you get a resolution conflict that only appears at assemble time.

dependencyDashboardApproval stays true — inherited from the top level and restated here so it survives someone reordering these rules. A native bump cannot be judged by CI: nothing in this repo builds an APK or an .ipa (see ci.yml), so the only real verification is a device or emulator build, which is a human act. That is the reason to gate them, NOT a reason to hide them — the point of narrowing ignorePaths is that vulnerabilityAlerts, which opts out of this gate, can now reach them at all.
Action digests are pinned for supply-chain reasons (see .github/actions/setup/action.yml); this is what keeps the pins from rotting.

It also sets automerge false, although no rule automerges today, so a patch automerge added later cannot reach it. A pinned action reads `owner/action@<sha> # v7.0.1`, so a v7.0.1 to v7.0.2 bump is updateType 'patch' — but unlike a library patch it repoints a SHA at new third-party code that runs inside CI, including release.yml, whose environment holds the signing certificates. Merging that unattended is precisely the exposure the digest pinning exists to prevent (see .github/actions/setup/action.yml). These stay behind a tick and a human.
The empty additionalBranchPrefix keeps digest bumps, most of them 'patch' updates, in the 'github actions' group branch rather than splitting them onto renovate/patch-*.

Shipped runtime code where a patch can change what users run: the HTML sanitizer, the maths renderer (KaTeX parses untrusted LaTeX into markup), the Matrix SDK with its crypto WASM, the widget API and the desktop Chromium. Their patches set automerge false, although no rule automerges today, so a patch automerge added later cannot reach them. Like every patch they skip the dashboard gate, so a patch opens a pull request straight away and waits for a human merge. Their other updates follow the top-level rules unchanged.

additionalBranchPrefix 'runtime-' gives these patches branches of their own: off renovate/patch-* and off the branch of a minor or major in the same group that is waiting for dashboard approval. electron's patches therefore leave the 'electron shell' group's patch branch for renovate/runtime-electron-shell.
Keep this rule LAST: the last matching rule wins each key, and it must win automerge over any earlier rule. scripts/renovate-config.spec.mjs checks that no later rule sets automerge.
